root.title: Opt-in request correlation
root.objective: Plan an integrated, compatibility-preserving request-correlation feature without asserting implementation or runtime success.
concerns: Generated identifiers must use a secure platform primitive.
No runtime dependency may be added.
Existing middleware ordering and public compatibility must be preserved.

outcomes.description: The proposed integrated candidate will be checked for req.id and matching X-Request-Id behavior when enabled.
The proposed integrated candidate will be checked against the unchanged disabled baseline.
The proposal includes focused tests and public documentation responsibilities.

cut.rationale: Configuration, request identity, response propagation, tests, and documentation have distinct file ownership while requiring explicit end-to-end seams.

children.title: Opt-in configuration
children.objective: Plan application-owned configuration and dispatch gating that preserve disabled behavior.
concerns: Do not enable correlation by default.
Do not add a runtime dependency.

outcomes.description: Correlation behavior is explicitly enabled through application configuration while the default path remains unchanged.

children.title: Request identity
children.objective: Plan valid incoming identifier preservation or secure platform generation and expose the resolved value as req.id.
concerns: Use a secure Node.js platform primitive.
Keep request behavior inactive unless enabled.
Preserve the valid incoming X-Request-Id exactly.

outcomes.description: Enabled requests expose one resolved req.id from valid input or secure generation.

children.title: Response propagation
children.objective: Plan X-Request-Id emission from the request-owned identifier while preserving disabled response behavior.
concerns: The response header must exactly match req.id.
Disabled responses must not gain the feature header.

outcomes.description: Enabled responses emit X-Request-Id equal to the resolved request identifier.

children.title: Focused correlation tests
children.objective: Plan focused request and response tests for preservation, generation, exposure, propagation, and the disabled baseline.
concerns: Assert observable public behavior rather than private implementation details.

outcomes.description: Focused executable cases cover request identity, response-header equality, and unchanged opt-out behavior.

children.title: Public documentation
children.objective: Plan concise documentation of the opt-in setting, req.id, X-Request-Id behavior, secure generation, and unchanged defaults.
concerns: Describe only the intended public contract.

outcomes.description: Public documentation describes configuration, req.id, response propagation, and disabled behavior.

seams.purpose: Carry the application-owned opt-in decision into request identity resolution.

interface.promise: Request identity resolution runs only when application configuration enables correlation.
interface.compatibility: Disabled applications retain existing request and response behavior.

seams.purpose: Propagate the resolved request identifier to the response header boundary.

interface.promise: X-Request-Id equals the request-owned req.id value when correlation is enabled.
interface.compatibility: The seam remains inactive when correlation is disabled.

seams.purpose: Expose request identity behavior to focused executable tests.

interface.promise: Tests observe valid incoming preservation, secure generation, and req.id availability to handlers.
interface.compatibility: Assertions target public behavior and preserve the disabled negative control.

seams.purpose: Expose response-header propagation to focused executable tests.

interface.promise: Tests compare X-Request-Id with the resolved request identifier and check the disabled baseline.
interface.compatibility: Existing response behavior remains protected when the feature is not enabled.
